title: DevOps
summary: What DevOps is (version control, CI/CD, monitoring) and a safe main / dev / feature branch workflow, then you put your app live: React front end on Vercel, Edge Functions and secrets on Supabase, and the Stripe webhook pointed at the live function.
goal: Deploy Myflix to a public Vercel URL that logs in, loads data and takes a test donation, and ship later changes through feature → dev → main.
required: Part I: make sure your app(s) are ready for deployment and tied to Git or a cloud service: front end on GitHub, back end on Supabase
Part II: deploy your app(s), bring them live, and have something to demonstrate

steps.title: Make a dev branch
steps.detail: The lesson's workflow: main is what's live, dev collects finished work, and feature/* branches hold one change each. Myflix only has main. The instructors' notes say to create dev at the start of this lesson. Run this in ~/Desktop/codeplatoon/assignments/week-02/netflix.
steps.code:
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git checkout -b dev
git push -u origin dev
steps.doneWhen: github.com/cruzjay188/netflix shows both main and dev branches.

steps.title: Check main builds cleanly
steps.detail: The lecture's pre-deploy checklist (word for word below) uses client/; for you it's front-end/. If it doesn't build on your laptop, it won't build on Vercel. Merge dev into main first if dev is ahead.
steps.code:
# 1. Switch to main and pull the latest
git checkout main
git pull origin main

# 2. Verify the app builds cleanly (no errors)
cd client
npm run build

# 3. If you have a dev branch that's ahead of main, merge it
git checkout main
git merge dev
git push origin main
steps.doneWhen: npm run build in front-end/ finishes with no errors and makes a dist/ folder.

steps.title: Confirm no secrets are in Git
steps.detail: Part I: the front end lives on GitHub, the back end on Supabase, and keys live in neither repo. Only .env.example should match the search below. The lecture's rule: a VITE_ variable is bundled into the browser, so only public keys (Supabase publishable, Stripe pk_) go there.
steps.code:
git ls-files | grep -i env
grep -rn "sk_" front-end/src || echo "no secret keys"
steps.doneWhen: The first command lists only .env.example, and the second prints "no secret keys".

steps.title: Deploy Edge Functions and secrets
steps.detail: Vercel only deploys the front end. Edge Functions are a separate, manual deploy. Deploy every function in supabase/functions/ (tmdb, hello-world, process-donation, …). stripe-webhook needs --no-verify-jwt (instructors' notes). Then check the secrets (TMDB_API_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) are set. SUPABASE_URL and the service-role key are injected for you.
steps.code:
npx supabase functions deploy
npx supabase functions deploy stripe-webhook --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase secrets list
steps.doneWhen: Supabase → Edge Functions lists every function, and secrets list shows your keys (names only).

steps.title: Import the repo into Vercel
steps.detail: vercel.com → Sign Up → Continue with GitHub → Add New Project → import cruzjay188/netflix. Set Root Directory to front-end (the lecture says client/). Framework Vite, build npm run build, output dist. Add environment variables with your names: VITE_SUPABASE_URL, VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and VITE_STRIPE_PUBLIC_KEY. Then Deploy. If Myflix has URL routes by now, ask Claude for a front-end/vercel.json that rewrites every path to index.html (Ticked has one), so refreshing a deep link works.
steps.doneWhen: Vercel shows a successful deployment and https://<your-app>.vercel.app opens Myflix.

steps.title: Tell Supabase Auth your live URL
steps.detail: From the instructors' notes, after the first Vercel deploy: Supabase → Authentication → URL Configuration. Set the Site URL to your Vercel URL, and add it plus http://localhost:5173 to Redirect URLs. Otherwise auth links point at localhost.
steps.doneWhen: URL Configuration shows the Vercel URL as Site URL, with both URLs in Redirect URLs.

steps.title: Test the whole flow live
steps.detail: Lecture step 5: on the Vercel URL, sign up / log in, use the app, go to Donate, and pay with 4242 4242 4242 4242. The Stripe webhook already points at your Supabase function, which is the same URL in production. The lecture's slides switch to sk_live_/pk_live_ keys, but 4242 only works in test mode. Stay on test keys unless the instructors say otherwise (ask in #eagle_questions).
steps.doneWhen: A new row appears in Table Editor → donations, and you have a live link to demo.

steps.title: Know where to look when it breaks
steps.detail: After every deploy, check the lecture's three places: Vercel → Deployments (did the build pass?), Supabase → Edge Functions → Logs (errors?), Stripe → Developers → Webhooks (200 responses?). To roll back, use Vercel's Promote to Production on an older deployment.
steps.doneWhen: You've opened all three dashboards and seen a green build, clean logs, and 200s.

steps.title: Ship one change the safe way
steps.detail: The golden rule: never push straight to main. Make a small change on a feature branch, open a PR into dev (Vercel builds a preview URL for it), merge, then open a PR from dev to main to go live. Log the live URL in progress.md and in the Netflix project hub.
steps.code:
git checkout dev
git checkout -b feature/small-change
# make the change with Claude, then:
git add -A && git commit -m "feat: small change"
git push -u origin feature/small-change
# on GitHub: PR feature/small-change → dev, then PR dev → main
steps.doneWhen: The PR shows a Vercel preview link, and after merging dev → main the live site shows the change.

concepts.meaning: Building and running software as one team, with automation for testing, deploying and watching it.
Every push is tested and built automatically, so broken code is caught early.
Code that passes is deployed automatically. Here, a push to main makes Vercel redeploy.
main = live, dev = tested work waiting to ship, feature/* = one change in progress.
A host for front-end apps. It builds your React app from GitHub and serves it on HTTPS.
A temporary live URL Vercel makes for each pull request, so you can test before merging.
A setting stored outside the code (Vercel dashboard, Supabase secrets) instead of committed to Git.
Putting an older working version back live (Vercel: Promote to Production).
